translation: Now the Son of Man will come in his majesty, and all the angels together with him, to the great judgment. Then he will sit on the throne of his majesty, and all nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them into two groups, just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. Then he will place the sheep at his right hand, and the goats at his left.
essential_meaning: The Son of Man and the accompanying angels arrive for judgment.
The Son of Man sits; the nations are gathered and separated.
A shepherd separating sheep from goats supplies the comparison.
Sheep are placed to his right, goats to his left.
alternatives: Glory for majesty; peoples for nations; divide for separate; on his right/left side for at his right/left hand.
A consistent present-tense rendering preserves the Old English presents; English future makes the prophetic time explicit.
analysis_cautions: Six overt finite forms, not seven; the angel coordination contains predicate ellipsis.
ðēoda is nominative, and ealle is feminine plural here.
Scēap is plural in both selected occurrences; gǣt is accusative plural and gātum dative plural.
No inference that every future must use willan.
Hand is accusative in the bounded side-expression, which also occurs with static standað on unassigned line8; weak -an alone is not case-diagnostic.
